text:
nina: heads-up: found an odd behavior in the Go generator sample where Recv() blocks forever if ctx is cancelled while the auth layer is sleeping (exponential backoff). repro attached to the sampleapp tests. anyone seen this pattern?

lee: oof. is this the example that wires in a RetryAuth transport around http.Client?

nina: yes. flow: GenerateStream(ctx) -> auth transport intercepts 401 -> starts refresh+backoff -> mid-backoff the test cancels ctx -> Recv() never returns.

tom: that sounds like two problems: backoff not observing ctx, and Recv not watching an internal cancel channel. how does the stream implement Recv right now?

nina: it spawns a goroutine that copies http.Response.Body -> chunk channel and Recv() reads from that channel. cancel closes the chunk channel? we attempted to close it but the goroutine remains stuck on body.Read.

ara: Go net/http2 has known behavior where Read can block until stream resets. if the auth retry is holding onto the transport or the request was never sent, closing the response body won't help. we should ensure the request gets cancelled at the transport level.

lee: quick proposals:
1) make auth refresh respect ctx (select on ctx.Done during backoff).
2) expose Stream.CloseWithError(err) or Interrupt() on the stream to force-close the underlying net.Conn/request.
3) ensure Recv returns a well-documented error (context.Canceled vs net.ErrClosed).

nina: +1. for ergonomics I'd prefer an Interrupt-style method on the returned stream object rather than forcing users to hold the ctx and hope it propagates mid-stream. users expect a Stop() or CloseSend() equivalent.

tom: API sketch I'd suggest:
```go
type GeneratorStream interface {
  Recv() (*Chunk, error)
  Cancel(err error) // idempotent, unblocks Recv and signals server
  Close() error     // graceful close after draining
}
```
Cancel should set a 0/1 atomic and close the transport connection. Close tries to finish reading then close.

ara: also doc note: callers should not rely on defer cancel() in handler goroutines that might block on network I/O for long. show pattern with ctx with select and a separate goroutine that calls stream.Cancel() on ctx.Done. e.g.
```go
ctx, cancel := context.WithTimeout(ctx, 2*time.Second)
stream, _ := client.GenerateStream(ctx, r)
go func() {
  <-ctx.Done()
  stream.Cancel(ctx.Err())
}()
for {
  c, err := stream.Recv()
  if err != nil { break }
}
```
This makes intent explicit.

lee: test idea: add a unit that replaces refreshToken with a fake that sleeps in backoff but only returns when ctx done is handled. assert no goroutine leaks with t.Helper plus runtime.NumGoroutine snapshot. we have a helper package for leak detection.

nina: i'll add the test + update example README to show Cancel pattern. i can also make the auth helper use time.NewTimer + select on ctx.Done to be safe.

build-bot: CI job example/generator-interop flaky: reproduced timeout on linux-arm64 in nightly run 2026-03-20. opened ticket INF-5221.

tom: nice. one more thought: ensure the Go SDK doesn't hide transport details behind too many wrappers; if we add Interrupt/Cancel we must ensure internal http client exposes a way to CloseIdleConnections or cancel the in-flight request. maybe keep a cancel func on the request context and call that from Cancel().

ara: yep, store requestCtxCancel in stream struct at create time. Cancel() just calls it and then closes any leftover readers. that should win vs trying to surgically close net.Conn.

nina: plan: small patch to auth backoff + add GeneratorStream.Cancel() (optional interface) + updated onboarding snippet + an e2e/leak test. i'll send a PR and ping @devex for review.

lee: thanks nina, please add a changelog note about "stream cancellation ergonomics" so support can route customers.

nina: will do. PR shortly.

build-bot: linked issue: https://github.com/redwood-inference/redwood-inference/issues/5221
